newsitem.title: USA: PRESS DIGEST - Wall Street Journal - March 26.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Wall Street Journal - March 26.

text.p: The following stories were reported in Wednesday's electronic version of The Wall Street Journal:
* The U.S. Federal Reserve raised a key short-term interest rate by a quarter-percentage point, its first move in over two years. Economists think the Fed will raise rates more in coming months.
* The Dow industrials closed off 29.08 at 6,876.17, and stock and bonds gyrated after the Fed move.

* The Federal Communications Commission is planning to let stand a Michigan city ordinance which puts fees and rules on long-distance companies, cable operators, and others trying to compete with local phone companies.
* Federal Trade Commission investigators allege RJ Reynolds Camel ads target youths and are asking the FTC to bring an unfair advertising case against the company.
* A Conference Board survey showed Americans still feel good about the economy and job market.
* Lincoln National Corp is mulling a sale of American States, its property-casualty business.
* Toyota introduced a low-pollution hybrid system with an electric motor and a gasoline engine for cars.
* Federal prosecutors are trying to pin down charges they made in an alleged penny stock fraud case.
* A federal investigation in Texas is looking at Columbia/HCA's system of rewarding doctors who joined its network and patient referral.
* A study showed the average health maintenance organization copayment for doctor visits more than tripled between 1987 and 1993.
* Prudential Corp agreed to pay $4.65 billion for Scottish Amicable Life, outbidding to other companies.
* The co-chairmen of clothing retailer Barney's received a blow from a New York court in their bankruptcy case.
* Deutsche Morgan Grenfell Sir John Craven will step down as chairman of the investment bank.
* NASD said short interest on the Nasdaq stock market rose 6.2 percent to 1.44 billion shares.

* Heard on the Street: By creating garbage companies, then video and car-dealer empires, Republic Industries chairman Wayne Huizenga has made hundreds of millions of dollars for investors in recent years. Along the way, the hard-driving, 59-year-old Florida billionaire also has enriched himself and his friends in ways that even some fans question.

* Credit markets: The Federal Reserve's first interest rate increase in more than two years sparked a brief bond rally yesterday, but prices soon fell sharply as investors began to focus on the increased possibility that another rate boost will be undertaken in May.
